notes.lr-resolve-explain-bakery-price-cut: A is the only choice that helps at all, but the arithmetic is not airtight: a 10% cut with 25% more loaves gives ~12.5% more revenue if all loaves are regular; A only resolves this if the cheap small loaves also cannibalized regular-loaf sales. 'Most of the additional loaves' leaves open a reading in which regular-loaf sales held steady and revenue still rises. Consider tightening A (e.g., 'many customers switched from regular loaves to a new small loaf priced at less than half...').
notes.lr-resolve-explain-norland-textile-wages: E is the intended composition-effect answer (low-wage firms closing raises the industry average). B (much more overtime) is arguably defensible under an 'earnings' reading of 'average wage'; the stimulus's 'raised the wages it paid' points to pay rates, which excludes B, but a careful test-taker could see two answers. Consider wording the stimulus as 'average hourly wage' to close this off.
notes.lr-sufficient-assumption-veltrax-trials: E is the answer that closes the gap (no large controlled trials by anyone else). B is a tempting restatement of the premise chain but does not establish that no large trials were run. Clean, but note B reads as a very close paraphrase of the premises, which is slightly unusual as a wrong answer.
